dimension_justifications.soundness: The retained-state half of the paper is sound and independently re-derivable: every Store value in Table 4 reconstructs by hand from Table 3 and the printed format identity bytes(n,b)=ceil(n/64)(8b+4), and I reproduced 106.235/9.661=10.9965x, 136.235/9.661=14.1018x, 56.438/9.661=5.8416x and its exact factorisation 1.4912x1.4912/3.9174 decomposition, 3.7038x, 11.3073x, 14.0969x, 1.8823x and 6.5980x to the printed digits, all agreeing with the archived registry entry E-QCOMEM-60-VALIDATION-20260812D-A (9.660873 MiB, 14.101763x, mean F1 0.5423679, catastrophic counts 0/1/5). The new headline half does not hold to the same standard. Section 5.1 states that the Section 5.6 transient is 'not a Store sum and not additive with one', Table 1's own footnote repeats 'is not additive with Store', and Section 5.7 repeats it a third time -- yet Table 1, the abstract, the second contribution bullet and the conclusion are all the sum S*D+T(N) of exactly those two terms, taken from two different executions on two different cohorts (60-item archival Transformers panel and 8-item composition run) in a paper whose organising principle is that cohorts are never pooled. Table 1 additionally uses the native-dtype S=136.235, importing the FP32-GDN confound the paper isolates everywhere else; under the paper's own all-BF16 like-for-like convention (S=106.235) the crossovers move from 5.13/4.69/3.79/2.01 to 6.73/6.14/4.97/2.63 and the worked ratios from 2.42x/7.37x to 2.01x/5.78x, and that version is never shown. The four Table 5 medians carry no dispersion and a two-parameter least-squares fit, in the same paper that devotes 'What the dispersion does to all of that' to the lesson that undispersed point estimates misled readers; every deployment conclusion is proportional to the fitted intercept gap 706.23, whose uncertainty is unquantified. These are substantive gaps in the central new claim rather than presentational ones.
dimension_justifications.presentation: Structure, scoping and table apparatus are genuinely good: Figure 1's caption states which code path the drawing does and does not cover, Section 5.1's closing paragraph names which system produced which table, Table 8 gives a per-cohort authorised-claim/explicit-exclusion matrix, Tables 9-10 give per-target coverage, verdict, decisive witness and boundary, Table 2 prints all 52 intervals including the unhelpful ones, and Section 5.7 plus Appendix I enumerate the limitations at unusual length. Localised problems are real: the abstract is a single ~55-line chain of nested qualifications that is hard to parse for the actual result; the reader must simultaneously hold four memory denominators and four executions; Table 1 contradicts its own footnote; and the composition run of Section 5.6 -- the newest and most load-bearing evidence -- has no table of per-target coverage or verdicts to match Tables 9/10, so its ten-target result exists only as prose. Table 23 still labels the reference 'Q16' after Section 4.2 states 'We write native dtype, not Q16'. Readable and evaluable overall, with localised obstruction.
dimension_justifications.contribution: Novelty is explicitly and correctly disclaimed for the quantizer (Jacob et al. 2018 applied group-wise, FlexGen's form), the grouping and mixed-precision surface, the split-replay primitive (CoMem), and the quantize-an-intermediate-and-recompute thesis (XQuant), leaving the hybrid whole entry, its accounting denominator, and the FORKAUDIT ownership contract. Those are useful and honestly positioned. What they buy is narrow: one backbone, one hardware family, 60 items on two datasets, a -0.45 [-2.06, 0.99] F1 delta that is not selection-corrected, no latency advantage over any of four systems, a transient term larger than the exact cache at every measured fanout, an allocator result that ties the paper's own paged-prefix baseline and is worse on generation increment, and packed-path sharing of 4% of per-request state. The ForkAudit witness schema (Appendix E) is a real methodological contribution, but its packed-path application is unevidenced (see issues) and its increment over a persistent-base content invariant is, by the paper's own account, transition-time localisation rather than exclusive detection. Clear and useful, but incremental and of uncertain significance at ICLR scale.

paper_summary: Q-CoMem extends CoMem split replay to a hybrid (attention + gated-delta-network) LLM. An offline Write group-quantises, at 64-value granularity with BF16 scale/bias, the depth-j boundary residual together with the lower-layer full-attention KV and convolution/recurrent state a later query needs; an online Read dequantises that entry, keeps mutable request state private, replays the query through layers [0,j) and reconstructs the suffix. A companion component, FORKAUDIT, is a fail-closed, phase-indexed ownership trace with seven contract targets (plus three packed-entry obligations) over immutability, private ownership, tail copy-on-write, host-side call provenance, and cross-arm / cross-N semantic relations. The paper frames the result as total memory M_total(D,N)=S*D+T(N): on a 60-item Qasper/2WikiMQA cohort a frozen depth-7 Q4/Q4/Q8 policy cuts the retained term S from 106.235 to 9.661 MiB/document (10.9965x like-for-like, 14.10x against the stack's native dtypes) at -0.45 [-2.06, 0.99] mean F1, while a separate composition run measures the transient term T higher than the exact cache at every fanout in N in {1,2,4,8}, so the sum favours Q-CoMem only above roughly five warm documents at N=1 and two at N=8. Latency is adverse throughout against exact reuse, honest dense recomputation, SGLang Radix and the published HYPIC prefix cache, and the paper claims no latency, capacity, recall, edge or broad-quality result.
strongest_verified_contribution: The whole-entry retained-state accounting for a hybrid split-replay entry, which is the one part of the paper a third party can re-derive end to end. Table 3 gives per-component element counts at the cohort mean length, Appendix C gives the packed-size identity bytes(n,b)=ceil(n/64)(8b+4) and reports it holding exactly on 180/180 item-policy pairs, and every Store row of Table 4 then reconstructs by hand: 10*2*3.7180+30*0.0625+30*2.0000=136.235 for full prefix, 4.1828+2*1.0457+6*(0.0332+0.5312)=9.661 for the frozen policy, 20*1.9752+30*0.5644=56.436 against a printed 56.438 for the quantised exact cache. I recomputed all nine printed compression ratios and the exact factorisation 56.436/9.661=5.8416=1.4912x3.9174 and they match to the printed digits, and the archival registry entry E-QCOMEM-60-VALIDATION-20260812D-A independently carries 9.660873 MiB, 14.101763x, mean F1 0.5423679, the [-0.020365, +0.010756] split-relative interval and catastrophic counts 0/1/5, all of which agree with Tables 2 and 4. That is a genuinely reproducible capacity measurement with a traceable paired-bootstrap interval, and the width-confound decomposition that accompanies it is exactly the kind of self-correction reviewers should reward.
strengths: Numerical traceability of the retained-state result is excellent. Store is defined precisely (deduplicated sum of tensor-storage bytes one entry owns, by (device, data pointer, storage size)), decomposed per component in Table 3, and tied to a closed-form packed-size identity, so a PDF-only reader can rebuild every Table 4 Store cell without the artifacts. Every ratio I recomputed matched, and every quality number and interval I checked against E-QCOMEM-60-VALIDATION-20260812D-A matched (Table 2 archival block reproduces the registry's [-0.020365,+0.010756] and [-0.115615,-0.001713] exactly).

Denominator hygiene is exemplary. Section 5.1 names four distinct memory denominators (Store, the Section 5.5 post-priming allocator delta, the Section 5.6 CUDA-allocator peak above a pre-fork baseline, and the excluded process/NVML domain) and states for each what it excludes; Section 5.7 repeats the exclusions; Table 23's footnote even bounds the cross-runtime inclusion-rule discrepancy at 0.58% on the one object both stacks hold.

Which-system-produced-which-number is stated, not left to inference. Figure 1's caption says the drawn packed Read path is 'not on the code path behind Tables 4 and 22'; Section 5.1 says the deployment tables are Transformers-only while every primary FORKAUDIT verdict comes from vLLM 0.26 + Transformers on full-prefix BF16 PG-19; Section 5.5's opening paragraph and Section 5.7's fourth paragraph repeat the boundary. This is the single most common failure mode in systems papers and this paper does not commit it for its primary factorial.

The audit's trusted computing base is stated honestly and repeatedly. Section 4.4 names capture/replay, the mandatory-slot schema, slot-to-live-tensor binding and framework storage semantics as trusted, and excludes coherent omission/fabrication, transient writes between observations, compiled GDN, ATen/CUDA and device/driver execution. Tables 8, 9 and 10 carry per-cohort and per-target boundaries, Appendix I expands them, and the paper states that a pass is trace-relative and not security attestation. It also says the audit's increment over a persistent-base content invariant is transition-time localisation, not exclusive detection.

Evidence against the authors' own position is reported rather than buried: the transient term refutes the paper's published component-inventory prediction (Appendix C retains the refuted arithmetic explicitly); the allocator result ties the correct baseline and is worse on generation increment; the 54.5%/42.2% saving is relabelled as a controlled ownership factor against a full-copy control; sharing is 4% of per-request state; the eight-item panel's policy ordering inverts the 60-item panel's and the inversion is printed; the throughput column is stated to reconcile with no generated-token count; the -3.4122 interval's upper endpoint is called out as 0.0390 from zero.

The artifact-scope admission is verifiably accurate rather than rhetorical. Appendix A states that eleven components are 'recorded in the accompanying method-provenance table as not archived in any package'; method_provenance.tsv does carry exactly 11 rows flagged NOT ARCHIVED (M-QCOMEM-GROUP-64, READ-GREEDY, SPLIT-DEPTH, the three POLICY rows, POLICY-CALIBRATION, STORE-ACCOUNTANT, DEPLOY-STORE, BOOTSTRAP, PANEL-RUNNER), and the Reproducibility Statement states in the paper itself that Table 4 is 'replayable from archived outcomes and not re-executable today'.

Method provenance is dense and specific where it exists: the quantizer, dequantizer, pack codec, group size, Eq. 2 write enumeration, Write path, Read fork, lower replay, suffix seeding, greedy decode, split depth, all three bit vectors, the calibration knapsack, the Store accountant, the deployment accountant, the F1 scorer (with both disclosed deviations) and the bootstrap all carry file, symbol and line-range entries (M-QCOMEM-*).
questions: What is the composition run's evidence identifier? Section 5.6 and the Reproducibility Statement both say it is 'a further registered execution under its own identifier', and Appendix J Table 32's 'Composition run' row is the only row in that table with no path, alias or registry entry. It also has no entry in the 49-entry experiment registry, no row among the 70 claims in claim_evidence_map.tsv, and no method_provenance row for the borrowing/shared packed Read path it exercises. Please name it and ship it.

Table 4's operating-point block likewise 'comes from a separate registered execution under its own run identifier' that the PDF never names. The artifact registry has E-QCOMEM-60-OPPOINT-20260903A, but that entry lists only cluster paths (runs/qcomem/r45-d7d13-60item-20260903a/...), no source binding, no content hashes and no one-command replay, unlike the archival package. Will it be hash-bound and shipped, and will its identifier appear in the PDF?

Section 5.1 says the Section 5.6 transient is 'not additive with' a Store sum, Table 1's footnote says the transient 'is not additive with Store', and Section 5.7 repeats it -- yet Table 1, the abstract, contribution bullet 2 and the conclusion all report S*D+T(N). Which statement do you stand behind, and if the sum is admissible, what exactly does 'not additive' then mean?

Why is Table 1 computed only against the native-dtype S=136.235 rather than also against the all-BF16 S=106.235 that Section 5.2 introduces precisely to isolate packing from the stack's dtype choices? Under the like-for-like convention the crossovers become 6.73/6.14/4.97/2.63 and the worked points 2.01x and 5.78x rather than 2.42x and 7.37x.

Table 5 reports four medians with no dispersion and fits two parameters to them. Given Section 5.3's own argument about per-repeat spread, what are the per-repeat and per-item ranges behind those four cells, and what is the uncertainty on the fitted intercept gap 706.23 that every crossover in Table 1 is proportional to?

The abstract's -3.4122 [-8.4296, -0.0390] paired interval is the only Q-CoMem-favourable interval in the paper that excludes zero. The registry entry for the run it comes from states 'no paired interval exists between frozen depth-7 and full-prefix Q8', and claim C-QCOMEM-OPPOINT-EXACTCACHE-01's scope field states 'No paired interval was computed between frozen depth-7 and full-prefix Q8'. Which pass produced it, from which archived rows, and can it be added to the evidence map?

The abstract says 'every applicable FORKAUDIT target ... covered and passing'; the conclusion says 'passing all ten contract targets'. Appendix E allows a preregistered geometry to make tail safety not applicable. Were all ten applicable in the composition run, or fewer? Please add a per-target coverage/verdict/witness/boundary table for the composition run matching Tables 9 and 10.

Table 4's timing column is described as 'that run's recorded aggregates ... under a rule it did not record', and disagrees with Table 22b's medians (0.181 vs 0.161 s full prefix). If the aggregation rule is unrecoverable, why print those cells rather than only the block-(b) min/median/max?

The supplementary provenance files the paper directs reviewers to contain author-identifying absolute paths and eight URLs to a named company's internal job platform. Appendix J asserts that the aliases 'carry no ordering, date, or platform information, and no path here resolves to an external service'. How will the shipped package be scrubbed before it is posted?

issues.observed_evidence: The composition run is the sole source of Table 5's four transient medians (930.91/1062.73/1178.41/1713.15 shared, 286.44/427.49/752.09/1441.93 full-prefix, 954.09/1063.35/1393.28/1976.98 private), the three least-squares fits, the N=12.5 crossing, the 214.87 and 263.83 MiB sharing savings, the 4% sharing figure (2 of 16 tensors, 0.500 of 12.938 MiB), the ten-target FORKAUDIT verdict on the packed path, and -- through T(N) -- the whole of Table 1, the abstract's central regime sentence and the conclusion. It has no entry in experiment_registry.json (49 entries; I enumerated all evidence_ids and none corresponds), no row in claim_evidence_map.tsv (70 claim rows, none mentioning the composition run, transient allocation, fanout, total memory or the crossover), no method_provenance.tsv row for the borrowing/shared packed Read path (M-QCOMEM-READ-FORK covers only the private materialise-per-query fork and explicitly says the borrow/rebind/tail-COW discipline 'belongs to the separate vLLM paged implementation, not to this path'), and no artifact path in the paper's own Table 32, whose 'Composition run' row is the only row in that table that gives a prose description instead of a machine-readable source. Section 5.6 and the Reproducibility Statement both say the run has 'its own identifier', which the PDF never names.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper's entire revision thesis -- that total memory rather than retained state is the quantity to report, and that Q-CoMem names a regime rather than a ratio -- rests on four numbers no third party can re-derive from either the PDF or the repository. The Reproducibility Statement's opening sentence, 'Claims map to registered evidence identifiers', is false for this cohort. Under my access mode this is worse than a PDF-only gap: I have the provenance files and they do not contain the run at all, so the reader is left with an assertion of having executed something.
issues.required_fix: Register the composition run as a first-class evidence entry with a named identifier, hash-bound artifact paths, per-rank shards, the preflight gate and the blind contract replay described in the Reproducibility Statement; add a claim_evidence_map row per quantitative claim it supports (each Table 5 cell, the fits, the sharing bytes/tensors, the token-identity result, the ten-target verdict); add method_provenance rows for the shared/borrowing packed Read path and the transient measurement instrument; and put the identifier and artifact path in Appendix J Table 32 and in Section 5.6 in the PDF itself.
issues.verification_test: Grep the shipped registry and claim map for the identifier and for the literal values 930.91, 1062.73, 1178.41, 1713.15, 286.44, 427.49, 752.09, 1441.93, 954.09, 1063.35, 1393.28, 1976.98, 12.938 and 0.500; then run the named one-command replay and require it to re-derive every Table 5 cell, the three fits, the four crossover D values and the ten target verdicts from archived shards, reporting any drift as a defect exactly as the Reproducibility Statement promises.
issues.evidence_needed: A hash-bound composition-run package with per-rank shards carrying per-target coverage and predicate rows, ownership byte accounting, token traces against the published N=1 path, per-fanout transient fields, and a replay script.

issues.location: Table 1 and its footnote (p. 7); Section 5.1 'Memory denominators' (p. 6); Section 5.6 'Total memory, and the regime it names' (p. 8); Section 5.7 second paragraph (p. 9); abstract lines 30-35; Conclusion (p. 9); Table 8 'Composition run' authorised-claim row (p. 25)
issues.observed_evidence: Section 5.1 states that Section 5.6's peak transient allocation is 'a CUDA-allocator peak above a pre-fork baseline, not a Store sum and not additive with one'. Table 1's own footnote states 'The transient term is an allocator peak on this stack, is not additive with Store, and fixes no admitted capacity.' Section 5.7 states the allocator results are 'neither additive with Store nor evidence of higher admitted capacity'. Table 1 nevertheless computes S*D+T(N) for four deployment points and four crossover values, and Section 5.6 justifies it in one clause: 'Summing two measurements is admissible'. Separately, S comes from the 60-item archival Transformers panel (Table 4) and T from the 8-item composition run (Table 5); Table 8 authorises the composition cohort for 'peak transient allocation per fanout' and does not authorise a total-memory model, and the same table's caption states 'Cohorts are never pooled; each row supports only the listed inference'.
issues.why_it_matters: A paper whose central methodological discipline is denominator separation and non-pooling produces its headline result by adding two quantities in different denominators from two different cohorts, and prints a footnote denying that the addition is valid directly under the table that performs it. Either the footnote is wrong, in which case the paper's denominator discipline is weaker than advertised, or the table is wrong, in which case the abstract, contribution bullet 2 and the conclusion are unsupported. A reader cannot tell which, and neither can I.
issues.required_fix: Resolve the contradiction explicitly. Either (a) justify additivity: show that the CUDA-allocator peak above a pre-fork baseline and the retained Store payload occupy disjoint byte domains on this stack, measure the union directly at least at one (D,N) point, and delete the 'not additive' sentences; or (b) retract the sum: present Table 1 as a two-axis trade-off (S per document and T per request reported separately with their own denominators), state that no total was measured, and rewrite the abstract, contribution bullet and conclusion so the regime claim is framed as a conditional arithmetic model rather than a measured total. If (a), also state which cohort the composed quantity belongs to and amend Table 8's composition row to authorise it.
issues.verification_test: For at least one (D,N) point in Table 1, measure peak CUDA allocator bytes on a process that actually holds D warm entries resident while serving N concurrent requests, and compare against the predicted S*D+T(N). Require the measured value to fall within a stated tolerance of the model, or report the discrepancy and withdraw the model.
issues.evidence_needed: One executed multi-document residency run, or an explicit derivation with byte-domain disjointness evidence.

issues.location: Table 1 (p. 7); Section 5.6 (p. 8); abstract lines 30-33; Conclusion (p. 9); contrast with Section 5.2 (p. 6) and Table 4's two Store columns (p. 20)
issues.observed_evidence: Section 5.2 introduces the all-BF16 column precisely because it 'isolates packing from the stack's dtype choices' and states that 30.000 of the 136.235 MiB reference is FP32 GDN recurrent state in excess of BF16, so 'part of that physical saving is dtype narrowing rather than the Eq. 3 packing step'. Table 4 therefore prints both columns for every row. Table 1, Section 5.6 and the abstract then use only S=136.235 for the full-prefix arm. Recomputing the paper's own arithmetic with S=106.235 and the same fitted T(N): crossover D becomes 6.73 at N=1, 6.14 at N=2, 4.97 at N=4 and 2.63 at N=8 (against the printed 5.13/4.69/3.79/2.01), the D=20,N=4 ratio becomes 2.01x (against 2.42x) and the D=100,N=1 ratio 5.78x (against 7.37x).
issues.why_it_matters: The abstract's regime sentence ('above roughly five warm documents at low concurrency and two at N=8') and every worked ratio in Table 1 are stated in the one convention the paper itself identifies as confounded by the stack's dtype choice, and the like-for-like version is never shown. This is the same width/dtype confound the paper handles scrupulously for the 5.84x ratio, so the omission reads as selective rather than principled and materially changes the deployment guidance a reader takes away.
issues.required_fix: Add an all-BF16 column (or a second block) to Table 1 with the four crossover values and four worked points recomputed against S=106.235, and quote both conventions in the abstract and conclusion in the same way Section 5.2 quotes both for the retained term.
issues.verification_test: Recompute (S_full - S_q) D = (b_q - b_f) + (m_q - m_f) N for both S_full conventions and check that the printed table matches the recomputation for each; require the abstract's 'roughly five ... and two' to be accompanied by the like-for-like 'roughly seven ... and three'.
issues.evidence_needed: No new execution required; a re-analysis of the already-printed numbers.

issues.location: Abstract lines 46-49; Section 5.4 second paragraph (p. 7); Table 2 second block, row 'Full-prefix Q8 - frozen Q4/Q4/Q8, j = 7' (p. 17); Appendix B (p. 16)

issues.location: Table 5 and its fits (p. 21); Section 5.6 (p. 8); Table 1 (p. 7); contrast with Section 5.3 'What the dispersion does to all of that' (pp. 6-7) and Table 22b (p. 35)
issues.observed_evidence: Table 5 prints one median per (arm, N) cell for four fanouts and no dispersion of any kind, then fits two-parameter lines through four points and reports intercepts and slopes to five significant figures (809.68+109.76N, 103.45+166.28N, 790.50+148.38N). I verified the three fits reproduce from the four cells by ordinary least squares, and that every Table 1 cell and every crossover D reproduces from them; the crossover D is exactly (706.23-56.52N)/126.574, i.e. directly proportional to the fitted intercept gap 706.23, for which no interval is given. Section 5.3 devotes a headed paragraph to the lesson that undispersed point estimates concealed a TTFT maximum of 1.57 s against a 0.16 s median and a TPOT maximum of 404.01 ms against a 53.45 ms median, and concludes 'we print minimum, median and maximum per timing cell'. Table 5 does not.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper argues at length that its own earlier point estimates were misleading without dispersion, and then builds its new headline on four undispersed medians and an unhedged two-parameter extrapolation whose intercept difference determines every deployment conclusion. If the transient cells disperse anything like the timing cells did, the crossover D values in Table 1 and the abstract are not resolved by the data.
issues.required_fix: Print minimum, median and maximum (or the full per-repeat and per-item values) for every cell of Table 5, exactly as Table 22b does; report an uncertainty on the fitted intercepts and slopes; and propagate that uncertainty to the crossover D values and to Table 1's four ratios, or state that the crossover is unresolved by four points.
issues.verification_test: Recompute the crossover D under the extreme per-repeat combinations of the eight measured cells and check whether the ordering (Q-CoMem smaller total above D*) is stable; require the printed D* to be accompanied by that range.
issues.evidence_needed: The composition run's per-repeat, per-item transient shards.

issues.location: Section 5.6 (p. 8); abstract lines 37-42; contribution bullet 3 (p. 2); Conclusion (p. 9); Section 4.4 (p. 5); contrast with Tables 9 and 10 (p. 26)

That closure is the paper's answer to its own most serious scope limitation, and it is currently supported only by an assertion of having run something, at a level of documentation an order of magnitude below what the paper applies to the result it is meant to supersede. As printed the claim is not falsifiable by a reader.
issues.required_fix: Add a composition-run analogue of Tables 9 and 10: for each of the ten targets give mandatory-slot coverage, the replay verdict, the decisive witness, the applicable/not-applicable status with reason, and the boundary. Reconcile 'every applicable' and 'all ten' to one wording that matches the table. Add the run's frozen geometry (ranks, GPUs per fanout, schedule, aggregation rule for Table 5's medians) as a counterpart to Table 6.

issues.evidence_needed: Per-target coverage and predicate rows from the composition run's shards.

issues.observed_evidence: Appendix J states: 'Aliases replace the internal directory names used during development; they carry no ordering, date, or platform information, and no path here resolves to an external service.' The files the same appendix directs a reviewer to contain: 11 occurrences of an author-identifying absolute path in method_provenance.tsv ('NOT ARCHIVED in this repository (live implementation tree /Users/<author-surname-forename>/MacLLM-Bench/gpu)'), 11 occurrences of a cluster path of the form /mnt/.../user/<same identifier>/... in experiment_registry.json, and 8 URLs of the form https://qs2.devops.<company>.com/model/production/job/trial/<job>/<trial> together with job and trial IDs and dated run identifiers (e.g. mixed-validation-rlmain-20260812d, r45-d7d13-60item-20260903a). The PDF itself is clean -- I found no identifying strings in the manuscript text -- and the referenced prior work CoMem (Liu et al., 2026a;b) shares that surname as first author, so the combination is a direct deanonymisation path.
issues.why_it_matters: ICLR review is double-blind and the reproducibility statement promises the package as anonymous supplementary material verified by content hash. As snapshotted, the very provenance files the paper offers as its traceability index would identify the authors and their institution to any reviewer who opens them, and they contradict the appendix's explicit anonymity assertion. This is a submission-integrity defect independent of the science.
issues.required_fix: Scrub every absolute host path, username, cluster mount, company hostname, job/trial URL and dated internal run name from experiment_registry.json, method_provenance.tsv and claim_evidence_map.tsv before shipping; replace them with the stable neutral aliases Appendix J already describes, and record the alias-to-internal mapping outside the anonymous package. Then either soften or keep the Appendix J anonymity assertion, but make it true of the files actually shipped.
issues.verification_test: Run a scrub check over every shipped artifact for /Users/, /home/, /mnt/, http(s) hosts other than public dataset/model repositories, and any token matching the author surname or affiliation; require zero hits before the package is posted.
issues.evidence_needed: None; a mechanical scrub plus a check in the build.

issues.location: Section 5.5 'Allocator endpoints under a controlled ownership factor' (p. 7); abstract lines 58-62; contribution bullet 3 (p. 2); Appendix H 'Primary allocator endpoints' and Table 19 (p. 33)
issues.observed_evidence: The allocator result -- Table 19's four rows (4.901/4.920/0.019, 4.890/4.907/1.951, 2.229/2.843/0.019, 2.229/2.843/1.950 GiB) and the 54.5%/42.2% reduction quoted in the abstract, contribution bullet 3, Section 5.5 and Appendix H -- has no claim-map row carrying its values and no registry field carrying them. Searching the artifacts, '54.5' and '42.2' appear only inside an unrelated overhead claim's numbers, and 2.229, 2.843, 4.890, 0.019 do not appear at all. The nearest registry entries (E-RR2-OWNERSHIP-MUTANTS, E-MF-SUMMARY) describe 'allocator reconstruction' in prose but record no endpoint values; C-MEM-01, the only allocator-valued claim in the map, reports a different cohort and different quantities (2,857,268,224 B and 2,216,007,168 B) and is marked 'Internal evidence registry only; not used as a current-manuscript quantitative claim'.
issues.why_it_matters: A number in the abstract of an ICLR submission should resolve to a re-derivable artifact value. Here an evidence ID exists but no value does, so the traceability chain terminates at a package the reviewer is told to trust. The claim is also the one the paper reframes most carefully (a controlled ownership factor, not an optimised baseline), so the reader has a strong interest in checking the endpoints themselves.
issues.required_fix: Add the four Table 19 endpoints and the two derived percentages as explicit fields in the registry entry that owns them, plus a claim_evidence_map row with an extraction test that recomputes 1-2.229/4.901 = 54.5% and 1-2.843/4.920 = 42.2% from archived per-rank allocator snapshots.
issues.verification_test: Run the primary package replay and require it to emit the four (final, peak, generation-increment) triples per arm and the two percentages, matching Table 19 to three decimals.
issues.evidence_needed: The per-rank allocator snapshot fields already captured by the factorial, surfaced into the registry.

issues.location: Table 4 timing column (p. 20); Table 22 aggregation footnote (p. 35); Section 5.3 (p. 6); Section 5.7 (p. 9)
issues.observed_evidence: Table 22's aggregation note states that Table 4's operating-point timing cells 'are that run's recorded aggregates over the same 900 rows under a rule it did not record, so they are not the block-(b) medians (full-prefix reads 0.181 s there against 0.161 s here)'. The same note states that no generated-token count reconciles the throughput column of block (a), and that in the operating-point run reconstruction still misses recorded throughput by a median 7.6-18.8% per arm. Section 5.7 also flags that the eight-item dense TPOT of 648.75 ms equals its own TTFT to three digits while the operating-point dense arm reads 53.46 ms, 'a discrepancy we flag and do not reconcile, its shards not being re-analysed'.
issues.why_it_matters: Three timing quantities in the paper are printed while being explicitly stated to be unreproducible from their own inputs: an aggregation rule that was not recorded, a throughput column that inverts to no token count, and an unexplained dense-TPOT discrepancy of an order of magnitude between two panels. The disclosure is honest and I credit it, but printing an unreproducible number and labelling it unreproducible is weaker than either reproducing it or removing it.
issues.required_fix: Recover the aggregation rule from the run's own code or shards and restate Table 4's timing cells under a named rule, or replace them with the block-(b) min/median/max; either derive the throughput column from generated tokens and elapsed time or remove it and print tokens and time separately; re-analyse the eight-item dense shards to resolve or retract the 648.75 ms cell.
issues.verification_test: Require that every printed timing cell be recomputable from archived per-repeat rows by a stated formula, and that throughput satisfy n/(TTFT + (n-1)*TPOT) for the recorded n within a stated tolerance.
issues.evidence_needed: The operating-point and eight-item per-repeat shards plus the aggregation code.

issues.location: Section 4.2 (p. 4) and Figure 2 caption (p. 18) versus Table 23 and its footnote (p. 36); method_provenance rows M-QCOMEM-BASELINE-FULLPREFIX and M-QCOMEM-STORE-Q16-DTYPE-DEFECT
issues.observed_evidence: Section 4.2 states 'We write native dtype, not "Q16", for the unpacked reference, because that arm asserts no uniform width', and Figure 2's caption repeats it. Table 23 nevertheless labels the reference row 'Q16' three times, with the caption re-explaining that 'Q16 is the unpacked reference, BF16 for the residual and attention KV and the stack's native FP32 for GDN recurrent state'. The provenance row M-QCOMEM-BASELINE-FULLPREFIX independently flags this as a mislabel: 'Table 1 and Table 2 both label this row Q16/BF16, which the code does not implement for GDN recurrent state', and M-QCOMEM-STORE-Q16-DTYPE-DEFECT records the mechanism (quantize_tensor at bits=16 clones in source dtype, so FP32 recurrent state is counted at 4 bytes/element, +1.0 MiB/layer).
issues.why_it_matters: The paper corrects a real accounting label in the main text and in Table 4 but leaves the old label in the appendix table that a reader comparing against SGLang and HYPIC will consult, so the same arm carries two names in one document. Minor in isolation, but it is precisely the labelling error the revision set out to fix.
issues.required_fix: Relabel Table 23's reference rows 'native dtype' consistently with Section 4.2, Figure 2 and Table 4, keeping the explanatory caption sentence.
issues.verification_test: Grep the PDF for 'Q16' and require every remaining occurrence to be an explicit historical reference rather than a live row label.

issues.location: Section 5.7 first paragraph (p. 9); Appendix A first and third paragraphs (pp. 14-15); Appendix I (p. 40); Table 8 'H20 archival Store-F1 validation' row (p. 25); Reproducibility Statement (p. 10); abstract line 20; Appendix J opening sentence (p. 41)
issues.observed_evidence: The mutable-code-directory limitation is disclosed in five places -- Section 5.7 ('its launcher used a mutable code directory, froze no full-source or model-weight ledger'), Appendix A ('the original execution did not freeze a complete source or model-weight ledger; offline outcome replay therefore does not imply source-frozen GPU regeneration'), Appendix I, Table 8's authorised-claim row ('not source-frozen regeneration'), and the Reproducibility Statement ('replayable from archived outcomes and not re-executable today') -- and matches the artifact exactly (registry: 'The executed launcher used a mutable shared CODE_DIR and retained no pre-execution full source or model-weight ledger'; source_binding.preexecution_full_source_ledger=false). I found no place where the archival cohort is described in stronger terms than the admission allows: Section 5.2 correctly calls both columns 'exact re-analyses of the same archived rows'. Two residual weak spots: the abstract calls the cohort 'archival' without saying what that costs the reader, and Appendix J opens 'The source-complete primary package, derived summaries, raw ledgers, and expanded numerical sidecars are content-bound and locally replayable', where 'source-complete' is true of the ForkAudit primary package but sits at the head of the table that also lists the 60-item package.
issues.why_it_matters: The disclosure discipline here is a genuine strength and I want to record that it is verifiably accurate. The residual risk is that a reader who reads only the abstract and Appendix J's opening sentence carries away 'source-complete' and 'content-bound and locally replayable' without meeting the five places that say Table 4 is not re-executable.
issues.required_fix: Add four words to the abstract making 'archival' mean 'replayable from archived outcomes, not re-executable', and scope Appendix J's opening sentence to the primary factorial package by name.
issues.verification_test: Read the abstract and Appendix J's first paragraph in isolation and check that neither can be read as asserting re-executability of Table 4.

issues.location: Section 5.1 'Quality cohort and generation budgets' (p. 5); Appendix A first paragraph (p. 14); Appendix B (p. 16); references (Bai et al., 2024b;c)
issues.observed_evidence: Re-running the quality panel needs: model (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B revision 59d61f3), hardware (8 x H20-3e), stack (Python 3.11.13, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu129, Transformers 5.14.1, CUDA 12.9), cohort (Qasper/2WikiMQA source indices 6-35, 30 each, calibration 4-5), prompt (official LongBench-v1, 4,096-token cap, first-and-last-half truncation with a 256-token minimum), decoding (greedy, EOS stop, 128/32 new tokens by dataset), seeds and repeats. All of these are given except: the interpreter version for the archival run is stated to be unrecorded; the upstream LongBench dataset revision and evaluation-code commit were not recorded and 'cannot be reconstructed after the fact'; the archival bootstrap seed was not recorded, so those endpoints reproduce only up to Monte-Carlo noise; F1 is a reimplementation with two disclosed deviations; and the eleven components that select the operating point and produce the uncertainty (panel runner, launcher, layer-policy search, Store accountant, deployment accountant, bootstrap and aggregation) are marked NOT ARCHIVED. The composition run additionally lacks a stated rank/GPU layout and an aggregation rule for its medians.
issues.why_it_matters: Individually each gap is disclosed and each has a stated workaround (match the archived data hash rather than resolve an upstream revision; the generator, seed sequence and order-statistic convention are specified for the new intervals; five-seed movement is bounded at 0.075 points). Collectively they mean the paper is replayable rather than reproducible, which the paper says. The specific remaining blocker is the eleven unshipped components, which the paper itself identifies as 'precisely the components that select the reported operating point and produce the reported uncertainty'.
issues.required_fix: Ship the eleven NOT ARCHIVED components (panel runner and launcher, layer-policy search, group-size verification, Store and deployment accountants, greedy/timing driver, bootstrap and aggregation scripts) so Table 4 becomes re-executable, and state the composition run's rank/GPU layout and median aggregation rule.
issues.verification_test: Attempt a fresh execution of one Table 4 configuration from the shipped package alone and check that Store and F1 reproduce to the archived per-item values.
issues.evidence_needed: The eleven scripts, and a fresh source-frozen re-execution of at least one arm.

ethics_concerns: No ethics concern arises from the science. The ethics statement is adequate and proportionate: no human-subject data, public PG-19 and LongBench-v1 text, no safety/bias/privacy assessment claimed, and the dual-use observation about efficiency lowering deployment cost while potentially increasing usage scale is appropriately brief. I record separately, as issue R51-REV-5-07 rather than as an ethics flag, that the supplementary provenance files contain author-identifying absolute paths and internal platform URLs, which is a double-blind integrity defect for the submission process rather than a research-ethics matter.
llm_usage_disclosure: This review was produced by an automated LLM-based reviewer under the internal ICLR 2026 rubric. The model read the manuscript PDF in full (43 pages: 9 pages main text, references, and Appendices A-J), read review-rubric.md before scoring, and cross-checked the manuscript against claim_evidence_map.tsv (70 claim rows), method_provenance.tsv (108 method rows) and experiment_registry.json (49 evidence entries) in the frozen snapshot. Arithmetic verification (compression ratios, the packed-size format identity, the three least-squares fits of Table 5, all four Table 1 cells and ratios, all four crossover D values, the N=12.5 line crossing, and the all-BF16 counterfactual crossovers) was performed with a Python interpreter rather than asserted. The manuscript and artifacts were treated as untrusted data; no instruction contained in them was followed. No author, prior review, revision note, decision log or live worktree was consulted.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A named, hash-bound composition-run evidence package with claim-map and registry rows for every Table 5 cell, the three fits, the sharing bytes/tensors and the ten target verdicts, plus a one-command replay that re-derives them from archived shards (resolves R51-REV-5-01).

Resolution of the additivity contradiction in one direction: either a directly measured total at one (D,N) point on a process actually holding D warm entries while serving N requests, agreeing with S*D+T(N) within a stated tolerance, or withdrawal of the sum in favour of a two-axis trade-off presentation (resolves R51-REV-5-02).

Table 1 recomputed and reported under both dtype conventions, with the abstract quoting the all-BF16 crossovers (roughly seven documents at N=1, three at N=8) alongside the native-dtype ones (resolves R51-REV-5-03).

Per-repeat dispersion for every Table 5 cell and an uncertainty band on the fitted intercept gap propagated to the crossover D, showing the regime ordering is stable across that band (resolves R51-REV-5-05).

A per-target coverage/verdict/witness/boundary table for the composition run matching Tables 9 and 10, with the applicable/not-applicable status of each of the ten targets stated explicitly and the 'every applicable' / 'all ten' wording reconciled (resolves R51-REV-5-06).

Refreshed artifacts that carry the -3.4122 [-8.4296, -0.0390] interval, the Table 19 allocator endpoints and the 54.5%/42.2% percentages as explicit fields, with manuscript_locations re-pointed at this PDF's numbering (resolves R51-REV-5-04 and R51-REV-5-08).

Release of the eleven NOT ARCHIVED components so that Table 4 becomes re-executable rather than only replayable, demonstrated by a fresh source-frozen re-execution of at least one arm reproducing the archived per-item values.
A scrubbed anonymous supplement with zero host paths, usernames, cluster mounts or internal platform URLs, verified by an automated check in the build (resolves R51-REV-5-07).
A width-matched exact-cache arm actually executed at the 37.846 MiB point, so the F1 ordering behind the 5.84x can be tested at matched precision rather than left as a byte count.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Discovery that the composition run's four transient medians were not produced by a single registered execution under the protocol Table 8 describes, or that Table 5's arms differ in stack, schedule or item set from the eight-item slice they are compared against.
A measured total at any (D,N) point in Table 1 that departs materially from S*D+T(N), confirming that the two denominators are not additive as the paper's own three statements say.
Per-repeat dispersion on Table 5 wide enough that the crossover D is not resolved, which would remove the abstract's and conclusion's regime claim entirely.
Any of the ten composition-run targets turning out to be not applicable or open rather than passing, which would contradict the conclusion's 'passing all ten contract targets'.

Evidence that the -3.4122 interval was computed under a different generator, seed sequence, item set or reference arm than the one stated, given that two artifact files currently assert it does not exist.
Further PDF-versus-artifact value disagreements beyond the ones found here, which would undermine the traceability premise the Reproducibility Statement rests on.
review_limitations: Access was limited to the frozen snapshot: the manuscript PDF plus three provenance files. The research package itself, the per-rank shards, the replay scripts and any composition-run artifacts were not available, so 'no traceable entry' means 'absent from claim_evidence_map.tsv, method_provenance.tsv and experiment_registry.json in this snapshot', not proof that no such artifact exists anywhere.

The two TSV artifacts and the registry carry timestamps earlier in the day than the PDF, so some disagreements (notably the -3.4122 interval and the 'width decomposition NOT yet in the manuscript' note) may be staleness rather than fabrication. I have scored them as traceability failures because a submission must be checkable from what it ships, but I flag the alternative explanation.
No GPU execution, replay or code inspection was possible; all verification was arithmetic re-derivation from printed values plus string- and field-level cross-checking of the three artifact files.

I did not attempt an independent novelty assessment of the quantization or prefix-caching literature beyond checking that the paper's own disclaimers (Jacob et al. 2018, FlexGen, KIVI, KVQuant, KVTuner, AsymKV, Palu, Quamba, XQuant, CoMem) are stated in the main text and expanded in Appendix G; a novelty-focused reviewer should assess the XQuant delineation independently.
